q: Compare last week's performance against this week and identify the likely causes.

checks.what: tool: compares against last week or same weekdays last week

answer:
Net sales fell: ₹2,78,950 (2026-10-12..2026-10-15, order-date) versus ₹4,68,721 (2026-10-05..2026-10-09) — a drop of 40.5%. This is large and driven mainly by far fewer orders, with ad activity and platform mix also contributing.

What changed (biggest impacts first)
- Orders collapsed: 251 → 147 orders (−41.4%), which by itself reduced net sales by about ₹1,95,782. Lower sessions and conversion were the upstream volume drivers.  
- Ad spend was lower: total ad spend fell from ₹2,86,290 → ₹2,04,301 (−28.6%), reducing demand; Meta in particular saw a big fall in sales (meta net sales ₹2,71,250 → ₹1,17,358) and accounts for the largest platform-level shortfall.  
- Contribution margin and profitability weakened: reported net profit moved from about −₹72,404 → −₹931 (note: these are P&L basis numbers in the queried windows and reflect the period composition seen). The P&L lines show a large reallocation in contribution that magnified the net-sales gap.  
- Prices / AOV roughly stable: Net AOV moved slightly (₹1,867 → ₹1,898, +1.6%) and therefore did not offset the order loss.

Confidence & data notes
- Period compared: 2026-10-12..2026-10-16 (this week so far; 2026-10-16 is partial) vs 2026-10-05..2026-10-09 (prior week). Data as-of 2026-10-16; some tax fields failed to fetch but the headline totals and P&L breakdown reconcile exactly. Partial-day caution: 2026-10-16 is incomplete.

Worth checking:
- Run a drilldown of orders and ad performance by ad_platform → campaign (Meta vs Google and top campaigns) to confirm whether paused budgets/creative changes or platform delivery explain the ad spend and order drops.
